target_customer: Healthcare providers and practices (free for most), with revenue from trial sponsors and sites that need patients
problem: Few patients learn about clinical trials they could join, which slows patient recruitment for drug development. Novelcare scans electronic health records to match patients to nearby studies.
business_model: Free to most practices; trial sites and sponsors pay for patient identification, practices can earn revenue from chart review on some studies
product_category: Clinical trial patient matching from EHR data

founders.name: Ethan Bond
education: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, did not graduate
founders.background_notes: YC page says product strategist at Palantir, helped build its life sciences division; product designer and software engineer by training.

founders.name: Jason Marmon
previous_startups: Skylight (NYC real estate app, acquired by Common Living)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led the Data Governance product team at Palantir and is a 2015 Thiel Fellow.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs EHR integration and eligibility criteria parsing across messy clinical data, standard engineering with hard data access and privacy parts. Founders came from Palantir life sciences.

defensibility.rationale: EHR integrations could create some lock-in, but matching logic is replicable and no data moat is documented in sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found describing an incumbent response to Novelcare.

market_need_then: The company cites that 72% of doctors want to inform patients of trials but only 5% do, and calls patient recruitment the primary bottleneck in drug development. These are company claims.

branding.domain_note: Uses novelcare.com, an exact match com.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material about the brand was found in searches.

outcome_analysis: Novelcare is listed Active with a team of five and no found coverage of funding, exits or shutdowns.
